content: Mastalgia, commonly referred to as breast pain, is typically a benign condition that often affects young women. This condition is primarily associated with hormonal fluctuations that occur during the menstrual cycle. During the menstrual cycle, hormonal changes can cause the breasts to swell, become tender, and develop a lumpy texture. Instead of discharging the excess fluid that accumulates in the breast tissue during this time, the body reabsorbs it, which can lead to discomfort or pain in the breasts. To ensure that no underlying issues are present, it is essential to perform a thorough breast examination and, if necessary, conduct a breast ultrasound to rule out any hidden abnormalities. Breast pain can be classified into two primary clinical patterns: cyclical mastalgia, which is related to the menstrual cycle, and non-cyclical mastalgia, which is unrelated to hormonal changes. In terms of prevention, there is no definitive way to completely avoid most types of breast pain. However, wearing a well-fitting and supportive bra may provide some relief and help manage the discomfort.
